messages:
Morgan: Heads-up — ran a 2h perf profile on canary yesterday. Seeing weird tail latency spikes on small-batch gen requests. KV hit rate drops from ~98% -> ~40% when the runtime switches kernels. Putting up raw logs + a flame in S3, TL;DR: seems correlated with kernel/quantization flips. Anyone seen this pattern?

Alex: can you paste the perf trace or a small snippet? curious if it's a kernel swap or batching-window misfire.

Morgan: pasted the short trace here: https://perf.internal/runs/1768999 (full flame in S3). Key observations: under low load kernel=A_opt, batch size≈1. Under short bursts runtime picks kernel=B_fuse and batching rises to ~6-12. KV miss rate spikes right after the kernel selection event.

Rhea: hmm — are we invalidating any KV shards on kernel handoff? kernel selection currently triggers a model.reload(...) path which may reinitialize caches. that could explain the hit-rate drop.

Dan: I suspect it's also the batching heuristic. when we flip quant_mode (FP16 -> INT8) the execution path uses a different KV key prefix (we hash seq_len + exec_variant). so same logical prefix may map to different keyspace and miss.

Alex: short-term: add an instrumentation label for kernel_variant and quant_mode on per-request metrics so we can correlate. but watch cardinality — don't attach input-derived labels.

perf-bot: note — prometheus ingestion has practical label cardinality limits. prefer aggregated labels and histograms rather than freeform high-card tags. :robot_face:

Morgan: operational proposal:
- console widgets: (1) token-waterfall with kernel-striping (per-token bars annotated when kernel/how kernel changed), (2) kv-hit heatmap per-route over 5m windows, (3) batch-size scatter vs p99 latency + regression overlay.
- correlation: emit ephemeral req_id -> trace_id mapping for sampled requests and expose a "jump to trace" in the console UI. avoid emitting trace_id as a persistent metric label.

Rhea: doable. example instrumentation pattern I'm thinking:
```
metrics.histogram('token_latency_ms', lat_ms, labels={'route': route, 'kernel_variant': kv})
if sampled:
  event.emit('trace_index', { 'req_id': req_id, 'trace_id': trace_id, 'ts': now })
```
This avoids trace_id as a prometheus label but still lets the console link to traces for sampled points.

Dan: alternative (reduces event traffic): keep metrics label-clean and implement an ephemeral lookup index (redis) with TTL=300s mapping req_id -> trace_id. console resolves on click. Pros: no additional metric labels, small storage only for a few minutes.

Alex: +1 to redis index. We'll do both: indexed lookup for interactive correlation and sampled metric labels for automated dashboards when we need aggregate grouping by kernel_variant.

Morgan: perf regressions summary: after kernel patch 2.1 p99 for search-route up ~18%, median stable. I uploaded diffs to S3 and added a short CSV. Action items:
- Rhea: add kernel_variant label to token-level histograms and add a feature flag to toggle (due EOD Wed)
- Dan: prototype ephemeral redis trace index and a small API the console can call (due Fri)
- Alex: design the three widgets and post mocks in #eng-runtime-design (sprint planning)

Rhea: EOD Wed works. I'll gate the label behind a config so we can flip it on only for diagnostics.

Dan: prototyping now — plan: use key `perf:trace_idx:{minute}` -> map of req_id->trace_id, TTL 300s. small footprint, cheap to rotate.

Alex: I'll add an explain tooltip in the widget that shows why kernel flips can eject KV prefixes and cause temporary misses. will mock the waterfall with kernel-change markers.

Morgan: thanks — if infra can bump the label quota for a short test window next week, that would help validate additive labels.

Ops: @Morgan INF ticket opened: INF-7342 to temporarily raise label quota for a 2h window next Tue. :white_check_mark:

Morgan: perfect. I'll follow up with a short run plan and identify a few synthetic scenarios to trigger kernel switches so we can debug in a controlled way. cheers!
